To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Student access time series generated for a course from Moodle logs can be used for successful prediction of final results in blended-learning courses and that if time series are transformed to frequency domain, using DFT, the resulting periodogram and DFT coefficients can serve as input for the modelling algorithms commonly used for this purpose.
the information sufficient for student performance prediction can be extracted from Moodle log files and that the information is preserved if log file data are transformed into frequency domain.

1) the student access time series contain information sufficient for the prediction of final results in blended courses and 2) by transforming time series into frequency domain, by using DTF, the amount of data needed for modelling can be drastically reduced without significant reduction of the accuracy of calculated models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to the problem of student performance prediction in e-learning environments by using the data automatically logged by the learning management system (LMS).
the question whether it is possible to use DFT coefficients in time series generated from log files for prediction of student final performance.

the following question: Can student access time series be compressed by means of DFT and still retain the information sufficient for successful modelling of student final grades in blended learning courses?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach to student performance prediction can be successfully applied to blended learning courses, especially for those with lengthy duration, and it can be used for the purpose of the course optimization and improvement.
the proposed method is suitable for the prediction of student performance and can be used for the improvement of the learning process in blended learning environment.
the use of DFT coefficients is not only a viable but also a promising approach for student performance modelling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methodology can be successfully applied for student performance prediction and it can be used as an additional tool in blended learning courses.
the proposed approach for student performance modelling can be used as an additional tool to help instructors and course designers in the process of course design and improvement.
the data contained in the log files can be used for successful modelling of student performance and that this modelling can be successfully performed with a small number of DFT coefficients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to predict student final results by using only the data that are automatically collected in log files, which is very important for large-scale courses.
the information contained in Moodle log files can be used for student performance prediction.
by using DFT coefficients, the data can be reduced to a small set, and yet the accuracy of student performance models will be high.
